name: Re-export traders (Dubai / Jebel Ali)

problems.words: Stock is split across Jebel Ali, Al Ras and Sharjah and no one knows exact quantities
quick_ideas: Ask each warehouse for a count of your top items on the same day, so you see one true picture
Make one person own the combined stock sheet, so there is one version.

workzap_build.text: A multi-warehouse register showing live availability by location, updated as goods move.

problems.ask_first: How many locations do you keep stock in?
problems.free_stops: How movements are captured at each site is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write the same top items from each location on one notebook page today, so shortages and doubles across sites stand out.
Give one person a fixed evening time to collect quantity updates from Jebel Ali, Al Ras and Sharjah, so sales hear one stock position.

problems.words: A buyer comes to pick goods and we've already sold them to someone else
quick_ideas: Mark goods as held once a buyer confirms, so nobody else promises them
Check the stock sheet, not a phone call, before confirming.

workzap_build.text: Reservations on the stock register so confirmed goods are set aside immediately and released only when loaded or cancelled.

problems.ask_first: Does the double sale happen with fast-moving lots, or mostly when several salesmen are selling?
problems.free_stops: The hold and release rules are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many buyer pickups this week were promised from stock already sold, so the size of the double-selling problem shows.
Keep one hold list beside the sales desk and make one person update it, so pickup promises match what is really available.

problems.words: Old models of phones and electronics lose value every week they sit
quick_ideas: List items by how long they've been in stock, so the oldest are offered first
Offer the oldest lots to your regular buyers this week, before they lose more value.

workzap_build.text: Ageing alerts for fast-depreciating items, sent to you the day stock reaches set ages.

problems.ask_first: Is it a few old lots that sit, or a large share of what you hold?
problems.free_stops: Ageing thresholds per category are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the shelves and note which old models have not moved since last month, so slow stock gets named clearly.
Give one salesman the job of offering old models to regular buyers every morning, so ageing lots get attention before value slips further.

problems.words: Regular buyers order on WhatsApp voice notes in several languages and things get missed
quick_ideas: Reply to each voice-note order with a written summary for the buyer to confirm, so both sides agree
Keep one order sheet per buyer, so nothing lives only in a chat.

workzap_build.text: An order book per buyer that turns WhatsApp orders into tracked lines through to loading and container.

problems.ask_first: Which gets missed more, the quantities or the model details in a voice note?
problems.free_stops: The intake and confirmation flow are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many order details had to be clarified after voice notes this week, so you see where language and speed cause misses.
Give one clerk the job of writing each buyer order into one notebook before packing starts, so picking works from a clear record.

problems.words: We gave goods on credit to an agent and payment keeps getting pushed
quick_ideas: List every agent balance by age, so you know who to chase first
Agree who approves new credit for agents with an open balance.

workzap_build.text: A credit ledger with ageing and approval rules per agent, with reminders queued for the owner to approve.

problems.ask_first: Is it one agent who keeps pushing payment, or several?
problems.free_stops: Approval rules and reminder timing are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each time an agent payment date was shifted after goods were released, so you see which balances keep slipping furthest.
Give one staff member one notebook for promised collection dates and updates, so every agent follow-up lands on the same day agreed.

problems.words: Payment comes in many ways and matching it to invoices is hard
quick_ideas: Ask buyers to quote the proforma reference on every payment, so it matches an invoice
For questions about how payments may be received, talk to your bank or a compliance adviser.

workzap_build.text: Payments logged against proformas daily, with unmatched receipts flagged.

problems.ask_first: Which way causes most of the matching trouble, bank transfer, cash or cheque?
problems.free_stops: The matching rules are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which incoming payments this week took the longest to match to a sale, so the worst matching gaps stand out.
Keep one page for unmatched receipts and give one person the job of clearing it by closing, so fewer payments stay floating.

problems.words: Too much cash collected from walk-in buyers in the showroom
quick_ideas: Set a fixed daily closing and deposit time, so cash doesn't build up
Have two people count at closing, so the figure is trusted.

workzap_build.text: A showroom cash log with daily closing and deposit tracking, flagging days when deposit doesn't match sales.

problems.ask_first: Is the cash piling up over a few days, or building up through the week?
problems.free_stops: The closing and deposit steps are laid out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many times cash is taken from buyers before the drawer is cleared each day, so the busiest buildup period shows.
Give one cashier one closing sheet for every handover of showroom cash, so notes stop sitting between counters and desks.

problems.words: I don't know which market is actually profitable after freight and discounts
quick_ideas: Work out one recent shipment's margin to each main market, so you have a first comparison
Note which costs surprised you, so you know what to track.

workzap_build.text: A margin view by market, buyer and product, including freight and discounts per shipment, refreshed as sales are entered.

problems.ask_first: Which cost do you know least for each market, the freight, the discounts or the duties?
problems.free_stops: How costs are assigned to markets is worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare two recent shipments to different markets including freight and discounts, so you see which route leaves less room.
Keep one notebook page per market for extra costs that appear after the sale, so pricing talks use real landed experience.

problems.words: My salesmen keep their own buyers, and when one leaves his buyers go with him
quick_ideas: Move buyer chats to a company WhatsApp number, so the relationship sits with the business
Start a company buyer list, with buyers' permission, so contacts don't leave with staff.

workzap_build.text: A company-owned buyer database with purchase history and last contact, shared across the sales team.

problems.ask_first: Has a salesman left with his buyers before, or is this a worry for now?
problems.free_stops: Who sees what, and how the list is kept current, is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many active buyers only one salesman has spoken with this month, so owner risk from single-owner relationships is clear.
Set a fixed weekly handover where each salesman notes buyer status in one place, so the business keeps continuity when staff change.

problems.words: Buyers ask for photos, videos and prices of the same items again and again
quick_ideas: Gather current photos and videos of your main lines in one place, so salesmen stop reshooting
Update prices in one list, so everyone sends the same figure.

workzap_build.text: A catalogue with photos, videos and current prices that salesmen can send in one tap, kept up to date from stock.

problems.ask_first: Which request comes most often, the photos, the videos or the prices?
problems.free_stops: How the catalogue is structured and updated is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which item requests came again this week and how often, so you know what salesmen should keep ready.
Give one staff member the job of keeping the latest item photos, videos and prices together, so replies go out faster.

problems.words: We don't follow up with buyers who visited once and didn't buy
quick_ideas: List the buyers who visited recently without ordering, so none are forgotten
Give each one to a named salesperson, so follow-up has an owner.

workzap_build.text: Every visit and enquiry recorded, with follow-up reminders sent right away to the assigned salesperson.

problems.ask_first: Are the visitors mostly new buyers, or known ones who did not order this time?
problems.free_stops: The follow-up timing and steps are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many showroom visitors left without buying this week, so you see how much missed follow-up is costing attention.
Set one fixed time each afternoon for one salesperson to call back past visitors, so quiet leads stop getting ignored.

problems.words: Wrong cartons get loaded, and buyers dispute quantities with no loading photos
quick_ideas: Count cartons against the order before each container is closed, so errors are caught at the door
Photograph the loading, so you have proof if a buyer disputes.

workzap_build.text: A loading checklist with carton counts and photos per container, shared with the buyer on WhatsApp.

problems.ask_first: Does the wrong loading happen with certain items, or when the warehouse is rushed?
problems.free_stops: The checklist and photo steps are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each order line with the cartons waiting by the loading area, so wrong goods are spotted before the truck leaves.
Give one loader the job of keeping all loading photos with that day's orders, so disputes can be answered quickly later.

never_say: Anything on sanctions, restricted end-users or destinations, dual-use goods or export controls; that needs proper compliance or legal advice.
Help changing a declared destination, consignee, value or description; pi declines plainly.
Anything on hawala, cash couriers, splitting cash or third-party payments.
UAE VAT, corporate tax or free-zone rules; refer to a tax adviser.
Storing buyer passports, Emirates IDs, trade licence numbers or bank details; visa and labour questions are for proper advisers.
Promises that buyer demand will return; if there's a robbery or threat at the showroom, call 999 first.

sample_reply.person: We keep stock in Jebel Ali and Al Ras, and twice this month we confirmed goods to a buyer that weren't there. What can we do about it?
sample_reply.pi:
Sure, you can start on this now, and the first steps are simple.
First, mark goods as held the moment a buyer confirms, so nobody else can promise them.
Second, make the stock sheet, not a call to the warehouse, the only basis for confirming.
On top of this, Workzap could arrange: one register across both warehouses with live availability, holding promised goods until they're loaded.

Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're welcome to say no.
